Now let me reconsider a potentially important detail: The spec says quoted display name content is "any sequence of SP, HTAB, or visible ASCII characters". Visible ASCII typically 0x21-0x7E. But my content check allows 0x21-0x7e plus space plus tab. Good. But what about a non-escaped backslash? backslash 0x5c is visible; but backslash has special meaning: "a backslash escapes exactly the next visible ASCII character or HTAB." So any backslash must be followed by valid char. My loop: if c=='\\' consume next. So a backslash at end -> invalid. Good. But what about two backslashes: first escapes second (0x5c visible) -> ok, consumed. Good.

Now, find_opening_angle's quote scanning: if backslash at end i+=2 may exceed n but loop ends; closed stays False only if no closing quote found; actually if i jumps beyond n, while ends, closed False -> UErr. Good.

Now, one more subtle thing: In `find_opening_angle`, if the string has a quoted display name but then no '<' and no '>' it returns -1, then parse_address treats as bare URI; but contains '"' -> parse_uri fails -> UErr. Good.

Now I think it's fine.
